dedupe_keys.name: israel full cost benefit analysis of the deposit refund programme for beverage containers

description: This case study presents a full cost-benefit analysis of Israel's deposit-refund programme for beverage containers, under which buyers pay a deposit that is returned when they bring back empty containers. Doron Lavee of Tel Hai Academic College published it in Waste Management (online in November 2009). The analysis counts every cost element of the programme, namely storage, collection and treatment of empty containers, against all potential benefits: savings in the alternative treatment through waste collection and landfill disposal, cleaner public spaces, reduced landfill volumes, energy savings from using recycled materials, and new jobs. It draws on a wide range of data sources and examines some critical issues with more than one approach. The article is available online by subscription, and the abstract is free on PubMed. Coverage is national. Caveats: monetary values for cleanliness and energy externalities rely on assumptions that are not reproduced in the abstract, and the programme rules have changed since. The main finding is that the programme is clearly economically worthwhile, with savings in alternative waste management costs greater than usually assumed. Simulation uses: cost and benefit items for policy scenarios on packaging return schemes in waste system models. Related records: the Türkiye deposit system early implementation data (data-turkiye-deposit-system-packaging-doa-early-implementation) and the Colombia packaging extended producer responsibility study (case_study-colombia-packaging-epr-system-dynamics) cover similar packaging policies.
